quote: The five votes in favor did not meet the requirement for a super-majority, so the measure failed.
summary: The Preferred Scenario Map amendment failed during the August 19 council meeting, after midnight on August 20. Five votes favored it but did not reach the required super-majority. The contingent zoning item was not acted on.

source_name: City of San Marcos application notice ZC-25-13
quote: A Zoning Change Application from "Future Development" (FD) and "Character District 2.5" (CD-2.5) to "Light Industrial" (LI) has been submitted
summary: The notice establishes a zoning application for roughly 199.49 acres, from FD/CD-2.5 to Light Industrial. The submission date is unknown. Later hearing dates on this mutable notice are not treated as known in September.

quote: The proposed moratorium would temporarily stop new permits for industrial operations using more than 25,000 gallons of water per day.
summary: The Hays County judge proposed a temporary pause on new high-volume industrial water permits. This was a proposal, not an enacted rule, and provides county-wide context rather than a project-specific decision.

quote: The San Marcos City Council voted 5-2 early Wednesday to deny a request for a land use change
summary: The Preferred Scenario Map amendment was denied 5–2 at 2:14 a.m. during the February 17 council meeting. The zoning change was not heard or voted on. This report appeared after the vote and records the outcome, not a prior warning.

quote: Construction has halted amid the lawsuits.
summary: KLTV reports construction halted amid land lawsuits. The halt date is not stated, so the case table uses the publication day. This is a suspension that may resume; court rulings on litigation motions are not project-approval denials.

quote: Residents still protested the decision, with some arguing the project is a misuse of their taxpayer dollars.
summary: Residents protested as Sulphur Springs allocated money for data-center litigation. This reports opposition after the documented construction pause, not an adverse vote on project approval.

quote: The Planning and Zoning Commission voted 7-0 to recommend denial of the project
summary: Prosper Planning and Zoning Commission recommended denial 7–0; the Town Council had not made a final decision. The cited article shows September 2 as publication day; its 11:27 a.m. timestamp is an update. The event date is left unknown in this record.

quote: The town government noted that since White Rose Partners has withdrawn the items, the proposal for Project Tomahawk is now closed.
summary: White Rose Partners withdrew the proposal before the September 8 Town Council meeting. The town described the application as closed; this was a developer withdrawal, not a final council denial.

quote: residents erupted in opposition at Monday’s city council meeting.
summary: Residents opposed Data Factory’s proposed Athens facility at a city council meeting. The council tabled citywide definitions and regulations; this does not establish a vote against this project’s approval.

quote: The council voted on an ordinance banning data center construction during the meeting.
summary: Athens City Council approved a citywide ordinance defining and banning data-center construction by a 3–2 vote. This is an area-wide policy action, not a vote on any single project; it is recorded as context only.
